options.cost: about $13,340/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: Waiting costs ~$132,511 in lost checkout revenue and exceeds the 60s degradation tolerance (BIZ-9). Terminating costs only a 2-minute replay of the idempotent price_sync job (policy may_interrupt, BIZ-5). No protected settlements in flight (DB-7) and no change-calendar window blocks interruption (BIZ-6). Memory shows a similar batch_replayable termination previously restored checkout (MEM-4).

audit.report: A batch job (batch_replayable_price_sync, pid 19541) held an idle-in-transaction lock for 4 seconds, blocking checkout sessions and degrading success to 55% over 15 seconds. The Database Guardian initially proposed waiting, but a trade-off analysis showed waiting would cost ~$132,511 in lost revenue and exceed the 60-second degradation tolerance, while terminating the idempotent job cost only a 2-minute replay. Both guardians agreed to terminate the blocker in one round. The executor killed the session, but verification 38 seconds later showed checkout still at 26% success and a new blocker (pid 19651, same workload) already holding locks for 7.4 seconds, so the incident was escalated.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_price_sync job acquired a long-held lock while idle in transaction, blocking checkout traffic and triggering a termination that did not clear the contention because a replacement instance immediately reacquired the lock.
lessons: For batch_replayable_price_sync: add a pre-flight lock-timeout or statement-timeout so the job self-aborts before it can block checkout for more than a few seconds.

For batch_replayable_price_sync: configure the scheduler to not immediately respawn a terminated instance; add a back-off or health-check so the replacement does not instantly become the next blocker.
For batch_replayable_price_sync: instrument the job to emit a heartbeat or progress metric so the guardian can distinguish 'idle but working' from 'stuck idle in transaction' without manual probes.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian correctly switched from wait to terminate once the trade-off math (BIZ-9) quantified the revenue loss and confirmed the job was replayable; the Continuity Guardian accepted without objection. No round was wasted, but neither guardian anticipated that the scheduler would instantly restart the same workload, causing immediate re-blocking.
follow_ups: Ask the pricing team to add a lock_timeout/statement_timeout to batch_replayable_price_sync and verify it in staging.
Update the scheduler configuration for price_sync to include a minimum restart delay and a post-start health check before it acquires catalog locks.
Add a dashboard alert for 'idle in transaction > 5s' on batch_worker roles so future blockers are visible before they degrade checkout.

events.title: R1 proposes wait

proposal.rationale: The root blocker (pid 19541, batch_replayable_price_sync) has been idle in transaction for only 4.0s [DB-1]. Checkout is degraded (55% success over 15s [TEL-2], 77% over 10s [BIZ-3]) but the business tolerates up to 60s of degradation [BIZ-3]. Memory shows terminating a similar batch_replayable workload (inventory_reconcile) previously restored checkout [MEM-4], but that was a verified pact for a different job. Without workload registry, change calendar, protected settlements, or tradeoff data, the risk of terminating an unknown batch_replayable_price_sync job (replayability, cost, interrupt policy unknown) exceeds the risk of waiting a short period for the 4s transaction to complete.
proposal.expected_effect: If the blocker commits/rolls back quickly (typical for idle-in-transaction), locks release and the 1 blocked session proceeds, allowing checkout recovery within the 60s tolerance window. Database returns to normal without forced termination.
proposal.risk_assessment: Blocker may not finish soon (e.g., stuck in application logic, waiting on external call), prolonging checkout degradation beyond 60s. Terminating blindly could violate data integrity if the batch job is non-replayable or mid-settlement (unknown without registry/settlements probes).
